title: Refund amounts could go negative when discounts were applied twice
text: Fixed a bug where issuing a refund after two stacked discounts had already been applied could produce a negative refund amount, which Stripe silently rejected. Added a guard that clamps the refund amount to zero and throws if the requested amount is not strictly positive or exceeds the original charge.

title: Payment provider calls are mocked with a shared fakeStripeClient helper
text: All tests that touch the Stripe SDK use a shared fakeStripeClient test helper instead of mocking individual methods inline. This keeps refund, charge, and webhook tests consistent and makes it easy to assert on idempotency keys.

title: All monetary values are stored as integer cents, never floats
text: Every monetary field in this codebase is an integer number of cents, never a floating point dollar amount. This avoids floating point rounding drift when summing invoice line items or computing partial refunds.

title: Concurrent transfers between warehouses could double-count stock
text: Two concurrent warehouse transfer requests for the same SKU could both read the same starting quantity before either write completed, resulting in stock being double-counted as available. Wrapped the read-modify-write in a SELECT FOR UPDATE transaction to serialize concurrent transfers.

title: All DB writes to stock_levels go through the StockLedger service
text: No code outside the StockLedger service is allowed to write directly to the stock_levels table. This keeps locking and audit-logging behavior in one place instead of scattered across importers, transfer handlers, and alert threshold checks.

title: Token expiry tests use an injectable clock, never real time.sleep
text: Tests that exercise token expiry or key rotation windows use an injectable fake clock instead of sleeping in real time. This keeps the signing-key rotation and grace-period tests fast and deterministic.
